title: Seventy five men applied for 24 places.
description:
Seventy five men applied for 24 places. The advert asked for male college students for a study of prison life, paying $15 a day for one to two weeks from 14 August 1971.

A two week study ended on day six. Psychologist Christina Maslach visited, was troubled by how participants were behaving and being treated, and confronted Philip Zimbardo.

The guards were told what to create. Thibault Le Texier's 2019 paper quotes the orientation: We can create boredom. We can create a sense of frustration.

One guard said he was directed to act. Guard 11 wrote in 1971 that the team specifically directed him to act a certain way. On tape, the warden told guards: we need you to play the part of tough guard.

The book says they had no formal training. Zimbardo wrote that the guards were told primarily to maintain law and order. Le Texier argues they knew what results were wanted and how to achieve them.

how long the study ran, against a plan of one to two weeks.

Human nature, or stage direction?

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_experiment: read, first part verbatim. Established the advert (male college students, $15 per day, 1 to 2 weeks from 14 August), that seventy five men applied and 24 were selected, the two week design, that Zimbardo ended it on day 6, and that Christina Maslach confronted him about how participants were behaving and being treated.
- https://www.Gwern.net/doc/psychology/2019-letexier.pdf: read, first part verbatim (Thibault Le Texier, Debunking the Stanford Prison Experiment, American Psychologist, 2019). Established the orientation day of Saturday 14 August 1971, quoted instructions given to guards (We can create boredom. We can create a sense of frustration.), the warden quote (we need you to play the part of, you know, tough guard), the Guard 11 quote (specifically directed me (us) to act a certain way), Zimbardo's own account that guards were told primarily to maintain law and order, and Le Texier's finding that the guards knew what results were wanted and how to achieve them.
